knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Large spills are first contained and confined, with visible matter removed using disposable absorbent material. The other options skip containment or use a product the guideline rules out.
The kit's parts are disposable so that it does not spread contamination. Option B lists disposable items; the others include reusable or prohibited items.
The guideline makes the disinfectant step depend on the risk assessment, and it requires a TGA-listed product where a disinfectant is needed. Option C states that condition.

practicalCriteria: Learner handles a simulated small spill in the right sequence, with the required protective gear on.
Learner identifies each item of a spill kit and states why each one is disposable.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Assessor observation record with the time taken
Completed spill record for the simulated event
stopWorkCriteria: The spill is large, unidentified, or includes sharp or broken material and the learner lacks the protective equipment
The learner is asked to treat upholstery with hypochlorite or to put alcohol on a spill
The spill is in an isolation room and the learner has not been briefed on its precautions
